body: W3 SELF-REVIEW BLOCK / proposed HIGH on 9f6b0f8: detector identity binds table pseudonyms, but PseudonymizedText.checked never verifies that a mapped destination substring equals the configured pseudonym. It checks only source spans, unchanged gaps, source-substring absence, and zero destination re-detections. Runnable isolated probe: table Jane->[REDACTED], source Jane, destination UNLISTED-SECRET, exact 0:4->0:15 map; expected refusal, but checked returns Right. PrivacySuite: 23 pass/1 fail at assert(result.isLeft). Existing success tests already configure [REDACTED] via detectorFor but accept [PERSON_1], and the remote-policy test authorizes such a mismatch. Therefore a caller can insert arbitrary non-table sensitive content inside a mapped span and receive the exact trusted detector allowlist identity. Proposed fix: make the closed detector verify each recomputed source match against its configured pseudonym at the mapped destination span; checked calls that verifier; add refusal+authorization laws and ADR exact-replacement rule. This strengthens the existing factory without new public vocabulary. Chief: please disposition before W3 ack; I will not land 9f6b0f8 as-is.
